title: Prefix Sum: Overview
summary: Precompute cumulative sums to answer any range-sum query in O(1) time using prefix[r+1] - prefix[l].

sections.heading: The Intuition
sections.body:
A **prefix sum** is the cumulative sum from index 0 up to a given index. To find the sum of a subarray from index i to j, compute the difference between two prefix sums:

**sum(i, j) = prefix[j+1] - prefix[i]**

Example: For array `[1, 3, 4, 6, 2, 5, 8]`, the sum of elements from index 3 to 5 is `prefix[6] - prefix[3]` = 21 - 8 = 13.

sections.heading: Building the Prefix Sum Array
sections.body:
Construct a prefix array of size `n+1` where `prefix[i]` = sum of first `i` elements. This allows direct indexing without off-by-one errors:

- `prefix[0] = 0` (empty subarray)
- `prefix[i] = prefix[i-1] + arr[i-1]` for i from 1 to n

Time: **O(n)** to build. Space: **O(n)** for the prefix array.

sections.heading: Querying Range Sums
sections.body:
After building the prefix array, any range sum query takes **O(1)** time:

`sum(left, right) = prefix[right+1] - prefix[left]`

This is the core advantage: preprocessing once enables unlimited fast queries.

sections.heading: HashMap Variant for Target Sums
sections.body:
To count subarrays with a given sum `k`, use a hashmap to track prefix sums seen so far:

As you iterate, for each prefix sum `curr_sum`, check if `curr_sum - k` exists in the map. If it does, those indices form subarrays summing to `k`.

This variant solves "Subarray Sum Equals K" in O(n) time.

approach: Many range-sum queries on a static array
Preprocessing is acceptable for repeated queries
Counting subarrays with a target sum (use hashmap variant)

quiz.q: Given prefix array [0, 1, 4, 8, 14, 16, 21, 29] for arr = [1, 3, 4, 6, 2, 5, 8], what is the sum of arr[2:5] (inclusive)?
quiz.explain: sum(2, 5) = prefix[6] - prefix[2] = 21 - 4 = 17. Elements are arr[2] + arr[3] + arr[4] + arr[5] = 4 + 6 + 2 + 5 = 17.

quiz.q: Why do we initialize the prefix array with size n+1 instead of n?
options: To handle edge cases with negative numbers
To avoid off-by-one errors when computing range sums
To store the maximum element separately
quiz.explain: Size n+1 with prefix[0]=0 allows us to use prefix[j+1] - prefix[i] without special handling for i=0. The formula works uniformly for all ranges.
